headline: High: Continue’s default filesystem/MCP tool use can conflict with a local read-only repo, while prompt-injection and leakage risks are limited by A’s lack of runtime surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable docs-only list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject content itself. Agent B can read workspace files and use MCP, so if A’s curated content is copied into B’s context or a shared file, B could be steered by malicious instructions. The bridge is indirect and not default, so low fits.
conditions: IF A’s content is pasted into B’s prompt or a shared workspace file
IF B is configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep A’s list content out of B prompts
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Use a read-only workspace for reference material
Add a prompt prefix that treats external text as untrusted

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no runtime, while B touches source code and open editor buffers and can read/write the filesystem. That creates a local leakage path only if sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace; B’s network egress is broad, but the pair does not show a default path from A to external disclosure. Blast radius is limited by A’s empty data footprint.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the workspace B can read
IF B is connected to a model provider that receives editor context
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a separate repo for sensitive material
Restrict B to local-only model providers
Rotate any exposed API keys promptly

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or runtime capabilities, but B can write the filesystem and shares state with other instances via filesystem. Even though A itself cannot write, the pair still creates a mutable workspace conflict surface around B’s default behavior, especially if A’s repository is used as shared reference material. Uncertainty about A’s runtime means we choose the higher severity.
conditions: IF multiple B instances operate on the same workspace
IF A’s repository is mounted alongside B’s editable files
mitigations: Use one B instance per workspace
Mount A’s repo read-only
Avoid concurrent edits in the same directory
Enable external file-locking if available

D_cascading_error.rationale: A provides curated machine-learning resources, and B can act on file and MCP inputs. If A’s content is fed into B as authoritative guidance, B may propagate unverified recommendations into code or tool actions. A cannot execute actions, but B can, so the cascade is from A’s informational output into B’s operational behavior. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A’s content is used as an input source for B
IF B is allowed to act on suggestions without human review
mitigations: Require human review before B tool calls
Mark A-derived text as non-authoritative
Add a verification step before code changes
Limit B to read-only analysis mode

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source docs-only repository with no touched data classes, while B handles source code, editor buffers, and model-provider API keys. The main compliance issue is local handling of code and secrets in B, not a residency or regulated-data mismatch with A. Because A contributes no regulated data surface, the compliance risk is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in B’s editor buffers
IF B sends editor context to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Do not open regulated data in B
Use a local model provider for sensitive work
Review retention settings for the model provider
Keep API keys in a separate secret store
